```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(easyNIS)
```

HCUP's reporting rules prohibit reporting cells with 10 or fewer discharges
and require that reported estimates represent at least two hospitals. Follow
the terms of the applicable Data Use Agreement and institutional review.
Suppression is a review aid, not a guarantee against every disclosure path.

## Count data-frame cells

`nis_cell_counts()` counts unweighted discharges and distinct hospitals using
year-scoped hospital IDs. This invented fixture has a small cell and a cell
with support from only one hospital.

```{r counts}
records <- data.frame(
  YEAR = c(2020, 2020, 2020, 2020),
  HOSP_NIS = c(1, 1, 2, 3),
  group = c("A", "A", "A", "B"),
  estimate = c(2.1, 2.1, 2.1, 8.4)
)
cell_estimates <- dplyr::summarise(
  dplyr::group_by(records, group),
  estimate = mean(estimate),
  .groups = "drop"
)
cells <- nis_cell_counts(records, by = "group") |>
  dplyr::left_join(cell_estimates, by = "group")
cells
```

`A` is represented by two hospitals; `B` has one. Counts are unweighted and
the displayed `estimate` is only a made-up value.

## Suppress data frames

For data frames, provide the count column and any estimate columns to mask.
The default threshold is inclusive: counts at or below 10 are suppressed.
Cells with fewer than two hospitals are marked as such.

```{r dataframe}
nis_suppress(
  cells,
  count_col = "n",
  weighted_cols = "estimate",
  hospital_col = "hospitals"
)
```

The output masks the small count and associated estimate in `A` and identifies
`B` as supported by fewer than two hospitals. When a table has totals or
grouped subtotals, inspect them for complementary disclosure.

## Suppress a gtsummary table

For a `gtsummary::tbl_svysummary()` object, `nis_suppress()` reads unweighted
counts from the table's cards, masks displayed statistics at or below the
threshold, and marks the overall statistic in the same row. This route checks
discharge counts only; it cannot check the two-hospital rule.

```{r gtsummary, eval=rlang::is_installed(c("gtsummary", "cardx", "survey", "gt"))}
nis <- nis_open(nis_example(years = 2019)) |>
  nis_flag_dx(heart_failure = "I50")
design <- nis_design(nis, heart_failure, keep = c(AGE, FEMALE, RACE))
table_one <- gtsummary::tbl_svysummary(
  design,
  by = RACE,
  include = c(AGE, FEMALE)
)
nis_suppress(table_one, threshold = 10)
```

The masked table is a starting point for review. Use the data-frame route with
`nis_cell_counts()` when both the discharge threshold and hospital count must
be checked.

## Common pitfalls

> **Common pitfalls**
>
> - Suppressing only values below 10 misses the prohibited count of exactly
>   10; the default masks 10 and below.
> - A single-hospital cell needs review even when its discharge count is large.
> - Masking a cell can leave it derivable from totals, subtotals, or another
>   table. Review the complete set of planned outputs.

See [`nis_cell_counts()`](../reference/nis_cell_counts.html) and
[`nis_suppress()`](../reference/nis_suppress.html).
